The proposed non-planar printing approach achieved a 44x improvement in failure strength and a 6x improvement in stiffness compared to conventional 2.5D printing for a load-bearing mechanical bracket.
The paper uses liquid crystal polymer (LCP) filaments, which exhibit strong anisotropic mechanical properties depending on the print orientation.
The offset slicing method generates non-planar slices that are perpendicular to the maximum principal stress direction, unlike conventional planar slicing.
The stress flow rectification step resolves ambiguities in the stress flow vectors to ensure the generated print trajectories are homogeneous and manufacturable.
The stress flow propagation step extrapolates the critical stress flow vectors from the boundary of the critical regions into the uncritical regions.
The optimization framework considers both the stress alignment objective and manufacturability constraints, such as uniform layer height and line spacing.
The trajectory stress-alignment metric β measures the alignment between the maximum principal stress direction and the print direction at each point along the trajectory.
The paper demonstrates the proposed method on three benchmark geometries: the fork, bunny head, and topology optimization.
The average trajectory stress-alignment β̄ for the fork, bunny head, and topology optimization geometries were 0.94, 0.74, and 0.88, respectively.
The paper uses a 5-axis 3D printer and a liquid crystal polymer material to manufacture the optimized parts.

The slicing stress-alignment metric γ̄ for the proposed offset slicing method was significantly higher (around 0.96) compared to planar slicing along the X, Y, and Z axes (0.38, 0.98, and 0.87, respectively).
The paper's method generates print trajectories with a tight distribution of distances between adjacent lines, ensuring high-quality prints.

The paper's novel stress-aligned non-planar print trajectory optimization method considers both part properties (load case, material anisotropy) and manufacturability constraints (extrusion and machine dynamics).
The paper's approach aims to improve the mechanical properties of non-planar FFF printed parts by utilizing anisotropic materials such as LCPs or fiber-reinforced filaments.

The paper's main contributions include a novel stress-aligned non-planar print optimization method, a non-planar FFF printing framework for complex mechanical geometries, and the experimental application of the proposed method to achieve significant improvements in mechanical strength.
